disease_label_per_paper: Acute purpura fulminans complicating Neisseria meningitidis bacteremia
presentation_summary: 32-year-old man presented with sudden bilateral foot pain progressing up the legs, fever at home to 39.4 C, nausea, vomiting, dyspnea, cough and generalized myalgias.
Initial vitals: temperature 37.1 C, heart rate 126/min, respiratory rate 23/min, blood pressure 90/52 mmHg.
Initial physical exam had no erythema or rash and no meningeal signs, but bilateral lower extremity pain to palpation.
Initial labs showed WBC 1.7 x10^3/uL and lactate 5.5 mmol/L.

ICU course was complicated by DIC with platelets <45 x10^3/uL, LDH 848 U/L, PT 20.0 s, PTT 34 s, INR 1.6 and D-dimer >20 ug/mL FEU; later he developed rapidly worsening distal lower extremity purpura fulminans with pain out of proportion.
